class.name: MeshPacker
class.brief_description: Collapses every [MeshInstance] below it into as few draw calls as possible.
class.description: Walks its own subtree, groups the [MeshInstance] nodes it finds, and bakes them into a single [code]PackedOutput[/code] child made of merged [ArrayMesh] instances and [MultiMeshInstance] nodes. Two strategies are used, and [constant PACK_MODE_AUTO] picks one per group: - merging bakes geometry into one [ArrayMesh] with one surface per material. Best for many small, [i]unique[/i] meshes such as kitbashed props or modular walls. - instancing turns sources that share a mesh and its materials into one [MultiMeshInstance]. Best for many [i]repeated[/i] meshes, and unlike merging it does not duplicate vertex data. Sources are hidden rather than deleted, so [method unpack] restores the scene exactly. Packing in the editor writes the result into the scene file; [member pack_on_ready] does it at runtime instead. Sources are skipped when they are already hidden, have no mesh, are skinned (a [Skeleton] is reachable through their skeleton path), or carry blend shapes, since their vertices are not static. [b]Note:[/b] this only touches visuals. Collision shapes, lights and other children of the source nodes are left untouched and keep working.

method.name: get_pack_stats
method.description: Returns what the last [method pack] did: [code]sources[/code], [code]merged_sources[/code], [code]instanced_sources[/code], [code]merged_meshes[/code], [code]multimeshes[/code], [code]surfaces_before[/code], [code]surfaces_after[/code], [code]skipped_surfaces[/code] and [code]vertices[/code]. Empty when not packed.

method.name: get_source_count
method.description: Returns how many [MeshInstance] nodes below this one would be packed right now.

method.name: pack
method.description: Bakes the subtree into the [code]PackedOutput[/code] child. Calling it while already packed repacks from scratch, so it is safe to call after editing the sources.

method.name: unpack
method.description: Deletes the packed output and shows the sources this node hid. Sources removed by [constant SOURCE_HANDLING_REMOVE] cannot be brought back.

members.member: When above zero, sources are also grouped by which cell of a grid this size their origin falls in, so the result still culls per region instead of drawing the whole subtree at once. Leave at [code]0[/code] to put everything in one batch per material.
Stores the merged geometry with Godot's default vertex compression. Turn off if the packed mesh shows precision artifacts.
In [constant PACK_MODE_AUTO], how many copies of the same mesh it takes before that group becomes a [MultiMeshInstance] instead of merged geometry.
Which strategy to use. See [enum PackMode].
Packs automatically in [method Node._ready] when running the game, for subtrees that are built at runtime. Does nothing in the editor, and nothing if the scene was already packed there.
What happens to the sources once their geometry has been baked. See [enum SourceHandling].
Maximum vertices in one merged surface; a batch that grows past it continues in a new surface. The default keeps surfaces inside the 16-bit index range. Set to [code]0[/code] for no limit.

signal.name: pack_completed
signal.description: Emitted at the end of a successful [method pack].

signal.name: unpack_completed
signal.description: Emitted at the end of [method unpack].

constants.constant: Merge everything into [ArrayMesh] surfaces, one per material and settings group.
Turn every group of sources sharing a mesh into a [MultiMeshInstance], even groups of one.
Use a [MultiMeshInstance] for meshes repeated at least [member multimesh_threshold] times and merge the rest.
Hide the sources. [method unpack] shows them again.

Free the sources at runtime to reclaim their memory. Sources that have children are hidden instead so attached collision shapes and lights survive, and in the editor nothing is ever freed, so a pack stays reversible.
Leave the sources visible. The packed output is drawn on top of them, so this is for comparing the two.
